query: Super Micro auditor resignation accounting investigation delayed 10-K
normalized: 10 accounting auditor delayed investigation k micro resignation super

output.content:
**What happened:** Super Micro Computer’s FY2024 Form 10-K, covering the year ended June 30, 2024, was delayed while the company assessed internal controls and while an independent Special Committee investigated concerns involving governance, transparency, and financial-reporting controls raised by its then-auditor, Ernst & Young (EY). [[1]]

**Auditor resignation:** EY resigned on October 24, 2024, and Supermicro disclosed the resignation in an October 30 SEC filing; EY stated that recently received information meant it could no longer rely on management’s and the Audit Committee’s representations and was unwilling to be associated with management-prepared financial statements. [[1]] [[2]]

**Why the review mattered:** The Board’s Special Committee had reported interim findings to EY on October 2, but Supermicro said EY resigned before the review was complete and before the committee had obtained all relevant information. [[1]]

**Replacement auditor and investigation outcome:** The Audit Committee appointed BDO USA as EY’s replacement on November 18, 2024, while the Special Committee’s review—supported by independent counsel and forensic accountants—ultimately took more than three months. [[1]] [[3]] The company later said the Special Committee found EY’s resignation conclusions were not supported by the facts examined in the review. [[3]]

**10-K resolution:** Supermicro filed its delayed FY2024 10-K, plus the outstanding Q1 and Q2 FY2025 10-Qs, on February 25, 2025; it said no previously filed financial statements were restated and Nasdaq notified the company that it had regained compliance with its filing requirement. [[4]] [[5]]

**Important qualification:** Filing the 10-K and avoiding a restatement resolved the reporting delinquency, but it did not mean the company’s control environment was clean: BDO’s audit opinion said the FY2024 financial statements were fairly presented, while BDO issued an adverse opinion on Supermicro’s internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2024. [[6]]

**Bottom line:** The sequence was a serious governance-and-controls event—not a confirmed historical financial-statement restatement: EY’s unusually forceful exit intensified the issue, the company conducted a special investigation and changed auditors, and it eventually became current with SEC and Nasdaq reporting requirements, but the FY2024 control weaknesses remained a material investor-risk consideration. [[2]] [[4]] [[6]]
